HelpHub live ↗SIH planner live ↗SIH code ↗
How the moving person & scroll effects work +
  1. The person is particles, sampled from my photo. The figure is cut out of my rooftop photo (black sweater, sitting) with the background removed; JavaScript samples ~9,000 points from that cut-out (assets/person-mask.png) and re-draws them as teal dots on the fixed full-screen canvas (#person) behind everything — brighter parts of the photo become brighter dots.
  2. Scrolling is the camera. The figure is rendered about 3× taller than the screen. Your scroll progress (0→1) is mapped to a vertical camera offset, so scrolling travels down the figure — head, torso, legs, shoes — exactly like the reference site.
  3. The figure reacts to you. Particles near the pointer are gently pushed away and spring back; the whole figure sways a few pixels with the mouse, and every dot breathes with a sine wave.
  4. Reveals & parallax. IntersectionObserver adds a class as each section enters, fading it up. Photo cards carry a data-sp speed and drift at different rates, with the image inside counter-moving for depth.
  5. The ending wave is a second particle system — a grid of dots lifted by two crossing sine waves, animated only while it is on screen.
